chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about vessels of gold and silver, so he disliked them. I said, 'Some of our companions have narrated that there used to be a mirror for Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) clad in silver?' He said, 'No, and praise be to Allah. It only had a ring of silver, and it is with me.'

Then he said, 'When Al-Abbas was circumcised, a stick clad in silver was made for him, similar to what is made for children, its silver being worth about ten dirhams. So Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) ordered it to be broken.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using gold and silver vessels for eating and drinking in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the distinction between mere adornment and functional extravagance, noting that his silver-clad mirror was only adorned with a silver ring, whereas he ordered the breaking of a fully silver-clad stick given to Al-Abbas for circumcision to prevent ostentation. This hadith highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *israf* (extravagance) and the practical application of avoiding gold and silver vessels in daily life, even for children, to cultivate humility and distinguish from royal customs.
